IN RESPONSE TO POA COMMENTS

Thank you for the detailed review, and for the explicit invitation to point to the code.
・We have linked the relevant code (and we have pinned links to a fixed commit (branch v-next @ 1a5cd9d5) so the line numbers stay exact over time.)
・Thanks for the comments, we have updated our documentation and blog to answer these questions as well for users

Just for context the npm package @effectstream/wallets allows dev to to bot connected injected wallets .e.g, Lace/Metamask/etc via CIP-30 and/or transparently create local wallets in the browser. The local Cardano connector intentionally mirrors the CIP-30 method names (signData, getUsedAddresses) so existing app code runs unchanged - so on a first read it looks like a CIP-30 dependency, but it is backed by a key generated in the browser, not an injected wallet.
https://effectstream.github.io/docs/home/components/wallets here are the list of available local wallets as CardanoLocal - in-brower local wallet BIP-39 key pair generated and managed by the library. No extensions required.

WHERE EACH ELEMENT LIVES IN THE CODE
Open source in the @effectstream/wallets and @effectstream/concise packages.

1. Browser-based private key-pair creation
A BIP-39 mnemonic is generated in the browser (line 69) and the device
key-pair is derived from it (line 84) - no wallet, no server:
https://github.com/effectstream/effectstream/blob/1a5cd9d506e73907d61c381946a23ddf381b664b/packages/effectstream-sdk/wallets/src/cardano/local.ts#L55-L111

2. Explicit delegation of permissions to that key
The player's main Cardano wallet and the browser-generated device key each sign the same link message ("link:<account_id>:<address>:<is_primary>"). That links the device address to the player's account, and from then on the state machine admits the device key's non-financial inputs as that player. NOTE: Due to short timelines for this project, we have submitted this milestone before the previous was approved. This was discussed with the Cardano Directive, and a formal statement was added at the end of the PoA. This milestone is totally independent and does not depend in any way on M1, M2 or M3.
BRIEF
This milestone delivers social login for wallets: a user signs in with an account they already have (Google), and gets a real multi-chain wallet - no seed phrase to write down. The design is a 2-of-3 secret: a 256-bit master secret is split into shares where any two reconstruct it and any single share is useless alone. One share is stored in the user's Google Drive (via the OAuth sign-in), another stays with the user, and a third serves as backup - so the wallet is recoverable if the device is lost, and no single party (not Google, not a stolen device) can reconstruct it. Reconstruction happens entirely client-side, and from the recovered entropy the wallet derives standard wallets: a Cardano wallet with CIP-1852 payment and stake addresses, an EVM wallet, and a Midnight wallet. This is the second of three wallet milestones (device key-pairs, social login, biometric login), supported for Cardano and the other chains EffectStream supports.

NOTE: Due to short timelines for this project, we have submitted this milestone before the previous was approved. This was discussed with the Cardano Directive, and a formal statement was added at the end of the PoA. This milestone is totally independent and does not depend in any way on M1, M2, M3 or M4.

BRIEF
This milestone delivers biometric login for wallets: the wallet unlocks with the device's biometric authenticator via passkeys (WebAuthn) - no seed phrase and no browser extension. The wallet runs in a cross-origin iframe on its own domain, so the dApp page holds no key material at all. Registering creates a passkey with the platform authenticator; the passkey unlocks a root key, and the root key signs an authorization for a per-app access key - a clean, auditable chain of custody that the demo shows end to end: DID, access key public key, the root key's authorization with timestamp, and a message signed through the embedded iframe. Because passkeys are synced by the platform (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager), the standard passkey recovery story applies. This is the third of three wallet milestones (device key-pairs, social login, biometric login), supported for Cardano and the other chains EffectStream supports.

BRIEF
This is the close-out for Core integrations - bringing AI-powered gameplay and frictionless wallet sign-in to the Cardano ecosystem. The project delivered two things, both Cardano-first: Shinkai Quest, an on-chain game template where a deterministic LLM judges a player's free-form input and awards tokens on chain (the AI runs on the Shinkai server, which can be local or remote); and EffectStream Wallets, a Cardano browser wallet adapter (Lace, Eternl, Nami, NuFi, and others) with one-time session-key delegation across the device-key, social-login, and biometric paths, so a player signs once and then plays without repeated pop-ups. Everything is open source and public; the wallet work powers three public games on midnight.fun. The close-out video and report are below.
